summary: B-9, Qutab Institutional Area, Katwaria Sarai, New Delhi – 110016. ** Petitioners** The present petition has been filed by Petitioner No. 1 to Petitioner No. 13 (hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioners”) invoking the regulatory jurisdiction of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission under Section 17(1) and 17(3) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (“the Act”) and other applicable laws seeking appropriate directions with respect to amalgamation/ merger of the companies of Petitioner No. 1 to Petitioner No. 12 (hereinafter collectively referred to as “Transferor Companies”) with Petitioner No.13 (hereinafter referred to as “Transferee Company”) and their respective shareholders and creditors pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230 – 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the rules and regulations made thereunder (hereinafter referred to as “the Scheme”) and assignment/ transfer of transmission licences pursuant - _iv. Pass such other order(s) as are deemed necessary in the facts and circumstances of the case._ (b) In addition, the Petitioners cater to distinct geographical locations across India, the proposed amalgamation/ merger _vide_ the Scheme, envisages to consolidate the business for creation of a single larger unified entity, and reduce the approval by this Commission under this Petition is a Condition Precedent for the effectiveness of the Scheme. (h) The auditors of each of the Petitioners have certified that the accounting treatment in the Scheme is in conformity with the accounting standard prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act. The Petitioners have also placed on record a copy of the Auditors’ Certificate(s) with respect to the accounting treatment proposed in the Scheme as issued to each of the Transferor Companies and Transferee Company. (k) The Petitioners have submitted that the arrangement as proposed in the Scheme is in the interest of the shareholders, creditors and all other stakeholders of the Transferor Companies and Transferee Company and is not prejudicial to the interests of any of the concerned shareholders, creditors, or the public at large. 3. Learned counsel added that the CTUIL has also submitted its no-objection in relation to the amalgamation of the SPVs with the Transferee Company. The representative of CTUIL confirmed that CTUIL has issued its no-objection for the amalgamation/ merger of the Petitioner companies. 9.
